title: Joe Petit, Wooden Joe, Willie Cornish and Bob Lyons
summary: Morris discusses valve and slide trombonists Joe Petit and Willie Cornish, Wooden Joe's Camelia band and bassist Bob Lyons working for Uncle Jake's pawn shop.

story.theme_name: Trombonists: who they heard, admired and learned from
story.community_name: Talking trombonists: who played the slide and how

blocks.x: I was wondering about some more of the old trombonists like Joe Petit.

Oh, Joe Petit, he used to be a hard one, you know. He used to play with Albert Nicklaus. We called him Wooden Joe. Yeah. Them two used to be together all the time. That was their band. That band was named The Camellia.
Did Joe Petit ever play the slide or mostly vowel?

No, he used to play vowel. Then he tried to get the slide, but he played it. You know, he played it. Because once you play a vowel, you can get the slide part, maybe. Because you got the amateur and just that division you got to make.
Did most of the fellas play slide when you came up? You don't remember many of the vowels.
Well, no more than Joe Petit and Frankie Deucon.
Do you remember Willie Carnage? Did he play slide or vowel or what?

Wait, wait, wait. Well, when I know Willie Carnage, I believe he was playing slide. He was a big, tall fella. He used to be on Rapport Street around Uncle Jake all the time. Him and the... Wait, wait, wait. Him and the fella used to play bass. Well, the bass player used to work for Jake. Uncle Jake there. If you would want a bass or any kind of instrument, he'd go there and get it for you. Tell him Uncle Jake, he stands for you. Did you have any of Bob Lyons? Bob Lyons. That's the one. You sure get them there. Now, that's the one you used to work for Uncle Jake. Oh, yeah. Bob Lyons was the bass player.
Because Uncle Jake would have had a pawn...
The big pawn shop, yeah. That's his son's player.
